meta.title: Heritage - Social Studies Syllabus
meta.issuing_body: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (MoPSE), in collaboration with the Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)
meta.levels_covered: ECD A - Grade 7 (Infant and Junior levels)
meta.notes: Compiled from the official MoPSE 'Heritage - Social Studies Junior (Grade 3-7)' Teacher's Guide and National Syllabus scope-and-sequence chart. At Ordinary and Advanced Level, the equivalent/related ZIMSEC subjects are History, Heritage Studies, Geography, Sociology and Family & Religious Studies, which are examined as separate subjects rather than a single 'Social Studies' paper.
source_documents: Curriculum Framework for Primary and Secondary Education 2015-2022
Heritage - Social Studies Junior (Grade 3-7) National Syllabus
Heritage - Social Studies Junior (Grade 3-7) Teacher's Guide

rationale: Heritage - Social Studies embraces the Zimbabwean constitution, patriotism, national identity, national symbols, and factors of production such as land, capital, labour and enterprise. It encompasses the history, traditions and social qualities considered an important part of Zimbabwe's image. The learning area moulds human character and is the foundation of Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu. It develops a spirit of national consciousness and patriotism through interest and involvement in national affairs, conservation and ownership of national heritage, and builds critical thinking, problem solving, leadership, self-esteem, ICT and resource-management skills leading to social and economic development.
aims: Develop a sense of national identity, patriotism and pride in Zimbabwean heritage
Develop knowledge and appreciation of family, community and national history
Develop critical thinking, problem-solving and leadership skills
Promote awareness of learners' rights, responsibilities and citizenship
Develop an understanding of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services
Promote environmental awareness and sustainable use of natural resources
Develop competences in the use of ICT for learning and resource management
Foster respect for diverse cultures, religions and social practices within Zimbabwe and the region
assessment_objectives: Explain the significance of public holidays and other national events
Demonstrate ways of showing respect for self and others
Discuss norms, values and appropriate responsible behaviour
Differentiate between new and old means of transport and Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
Indicate how modes of transport and ICT facilitate communication among people and countries
Justify the importance of work and leisure
Explain key historical events in the family and local community
Compare the practices of their own community's culture and that of others
Identify appropriate shelter for humans and animals
Explain the need for equal opportunities for all citizens of Zimbabwe
Identify global environmental issues that affect livelihoods
Describe the production and marketing of goods and services

assessment.profiling: A profile/folio system is developed for every learner to capture attributes that cannot be measured by tests alone, such as soft skills. The folio comprises projects, written tests, assignments and practicals collated termly from Grade 3 to Grade 7. Observation schedules, checklists and project tasks may be set at school, cluster, district and national levels.
assessment.inclusivity_principle: Arrangements, accommodations and modifications must be visible in both continuous and summative assessment to enable candidates with special needs to access assessment.

zimbabwe_specific_content_for_primary_le.note: This section provides detailed, factual Zimbabwean content that primary teachers use to teach Topics 1, 2, 3 and 10 of the syllabus (Identity, Cultural Heritage, National History/Sovereignty/Governance, and Global Issues) with real national facts rather than generic descriptions.

national_flag.adopted: 22 March 1980; first raised at midnight on 17/18 April 1980 to mark Independence
national_flag.designer: Cedric Herbert, based on the flag of the liberation movement ZANU(PF)
national_flag.description: Seven equal horizontal stripes, from top to bottom: green, gold/yellow, red, black, red, gold/yellow, green. A black-edged white isosceles triangle sits at the hoist (left) side, bearing a gold Zimbabwe Bird resting on top of a red five-pointed star.

colour_meanings.red: The blood shed by the people during the liberation war (Chimurenga)
colour_meanings.black: The black majority and African heritage of the people
colour_meanings.red_star: Hope and the nation's aspirations for the future (also linked historically to socialist ideals)
colour_meanings.zimbabwe_bird: The National Emblem; represents the country's history and heritage, taken from the Great Zimbabwe ruins

elements.shield: Green, displaying 14 wavy blue-and-white lines and a depiction of Great Zimbabwe at the base
elements.blue_and_white_wavy_lines: Water (associated with Victoria Falls), symbolising prosperity
elements.great_zimbabwe_depiction: The historical heritage of the nation
elements.kudu_antelopes: Two kudus support the shield, symbolising the unity of the country's different ethnic groups and the natural heritage
elements.hoe_and_rifle: Crossed above/behind the shield, symbolising the transition from war to peace
elements.wreath: Twisted gold and green silk, representing the mining and agricultural enterprises that support the national economy
elements.zimbabwe_bird_and_red_star: Placed above the shield (transposed from the flag) in remembrance of the people's suffering and a pledge to avoid its recurrence
elements.earth_mound_and_crops: Wheat, cotton and other crops at the base, representing the food and clothing the land provides
elements.scroll_and_motto: A white scroll below the shield bears the national motto: 'Unity, Freedom, Work'

national_anthem.current_title: Simudzai Mureza WeZimbabwe (Shona) / Kalibusiswe Ilizwe leZimbabwe (Ndebele) - 'Blessed be the Land of Zimbabwe'
national_anthem.preceded_by: Ishe Komborera Africa (1980-1994), a Shona/Ndebele translation of Enoch Sontonga's 'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika'
national_anthem.themes: The beauty of Zimbabwe's land, mountains and rivers; the sacrifices of the liberation war heroes; a call to protect the flag and the nation; a prayer for rain, good harvests and just leaders

zimbabwe_bird.description: A stone-carved bird, believed to represent an African fish eagle or 'the Bird of God' (Shiri yaMwari), sacred to the Shona/Karanga people who built Great Zimbabwe.
zimbabwe_bird.found_at: Great Zimbabwe National Monument, believed carved between the 12th and 15th centuries. Eight birds were originally found.
appears_on: Zimbabwean sports team badges and logos

national_flower.name: Flame Lily (Gloriosa superba)
national_flower.description: A beautiful, bright red and yellow climbing lily that grows wild across Zimbabwe.
national_flower.significance: Adopted as the national flower at independence; it is a protected plant in Zimbabwe.

national_geography_basics.major_waterfalls: Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya - 'The Smoke That Thunders') on the Zambezi River

unesco_world_heritage_sites.name: Great Zimbabwe National Monument
unesco_world_heritage_sites.significance: Largest ancient stone structure in Sub-Saharan Africa; former capital of a great empire.

unesco_world_heritage_sites.name: Khami Ruins National Monument
unesco_world_heritage_sites.significance: Capital of the Torwa State; known for its elaborate stone platforms.

unesco_world_heritage_sites.name: Matobo Hills
unesco_world_heritage_sites.significance: Area of unique rock formations, San rock art, and spiritual importance (Matonjeni).

unesco_world_heritage_sites.name: Mana Pools National Park
unesco_world_heritage_sites.significance: Wildlife conservation area along the Zambezi River with high biodiversity.

unesco_world_heritage_sites.name: Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya)
unesco_world_heritage_sites.significance: One of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World; shared with Zambia.

pre_colonial_states.name: Mutapa State/Empire
pre_colonial_states.notes: Grew out of Great Zimbabwe; controlled trade in gold and ivory with the East African coast

pre_colonial_states.name: Rozvi State/Empire
pre_colonial_states.notes: Known for stone architecture and control of much of the Zimbabwean plateau after the decline of Mutapa

pre_colonial_states.name: Ndebele State/Kingdom
pre_colonial_states.notes: Formed by Nguni-speaking migrants (mfecane migration from South Africa) who settled in south-western Zimbabwe (Matabeleland)

colonial_period.colonisers: The British South Africa Company (BSAC), led by Cecil John Rhodes, occupied the territory via the Pioneer Column in 1890
colonial_period.colonial_name: Southern Rhodesia (1895-1965/1980); simply 'Rhodesia' after the 1965 Unilateral Declaration of Independence (UDI) by Ian Smith's government

first_chimurenga_umvukela.description: First war of resistance against colonial rule, fought by both Shona and Ndebele peoples
key_figures: General Mtshane Khumalo (commander of the Imbizo Regiment under King Lobengula, victor at the Battle of Pupu, 10 December 1893)

second_chimurenga_umvukela.description: The armed liberation war fought by ZANLA and ZIPRA guerrilla forces against the Rhodesian government. It ended with the Lancaster House Agreement in late 1979, but Zimbabwe only became a fully independent country on 18 April 1980.
second_chimurenga_umvukela.outcome: Ended with the Lancaster House Agreement of December 1979 and the first democratic elections in early 1980. Independence was officially gained on 18 April 1980.

independence.significance: Zimbabwe became an independent republic on 18 April 1980. The 1980 date is the official year of independence.

robert_mugabe.significance: Founding leader of independent Zimbabwe. He left office in November 2017 and passed away in Singapore on 6 September 2019.

josiah_tongogara.role: Commander of the ZANLA forces during the Second Chimurenga (Liberation War).
josiah_tongogara.significance: He was a key military strategist and leader in the fight for Zimbabwe's independence. He was not a mathematician; he was a revolutionary soldier.

joshua_nkomo.role: Leader of ZAPU and founder of the ZIPRA forces.
joshua_nkomo.significance: Known as 'Father Zimbabwe' (Umdala Wethu) for his long commitment to the liberation struggle and national unity.

herbert_chitepo.role: First Black Zimbabwean lawyer and Chairman of ZANU.
herbert_chitepo.significance: He led the political wing of the liberation struggle from outside the country before his assassination in 1975.

mbuya_nehanda.role: Spirit medium and heroine of the First Chimurenga (1896-97).
mbuya_nehanda.significance: She inspired future generations to fight for their land, famously saying her 'bones shall rise again' before her execution by colonial authorities.

land_reform_programme.official_name: The Fast Track Land Reform Programme (FTLRP)
land_reform_programme.aim: Redistribution of land from a minority of large-scale commercial farmers (mostly of European descent) to indigenous Zimbabweans, addressing colonial-era land imbalances

national_heroes_and_heroines_acre.location: Heroes Acre (National Heroes' Acre), on a hill about 5 km from central Harare
national_heroes_and_heroines_acre.purpose: National shrine and burial ground for Zimbabweans who are conferred 'National Hero/Heroine' status for their contribution to the liberation struggle or the nation
example_notable_figures_buried_or_honour: Joshua Nkomo (ZAPU leader, first Vice President)

Independence Day

public_holidays_and_national_events.name: Heroes' Day

central_government_arms: Judiciary (Courts, headed by the Constitutional Court and Supreme Court)

national_languages.note: Zimbabwe has 16 officially recognised languages under the 2013 Constitution. Shona and Ndebele are the most widely spoken indigenous languages; English is the main language of government and instruction in most schools.

purpose_taught_at_primary_level: Identifies which clan/family group a person belongs to
Helps regulate marriage by preventing people of the same totem (often considered relatives) from marrying each other
Is usually an animal, part of an animal, or natural object (e.g., Shumba - lion, Nzou - elephant, Moyo - heart, Shava/Mhofu - eland, Ngara/Dziva - pool)
Is passed down patrilineally (from father to children) in most Shona families
Praise names (Zvidawo) usually accompany the totem and are used to show respect for elders

processing_tools: Duri and mutswi (mortar and pestle, used for pounding grain)
Guyo and huyo (grinding stone, upper and lower)
traditional_food_examples: Sadza (thick maize porridge, Zimbabwe's staple food)

child_protection_and_safety_zimbabwe.emergency_number: 116 (Childline Zimbabwe - toll-free for reporting abuse and seeking help)
key_rights: Right to a name and nationality

work_and_leisure_examples.importance: Work provides income and national development; leisure allows the body and mind to rest and improves social bonds.

currency_and_trade_notes.historical_context: Zimbabwe has used several currencies since 1980, including the original Zimbabwean dollar, a period of multi-currency use (mainly US dollars and South African rand) after 2009, the RTGS dollar/Zimbabwe dollar re-introduced from 2016-2019, and newer currency reforms since; learners are taught the general concept of currency, saving, budgeting and banking rather than specific exchange rates, since these change frequently.
teaching_focus_for_primary: Barter trade as a historical/indigenous exchange system before money

related_examinable_subjects_beyond_grade.note: From Form 1 onward, the content of Heritage-Social Studies is carried forward into distinct, separately examined ZIMSEC O-Level and A-Level subjects rather than a single 'Social Studies' paper.

subjects.name: Heritage Studies
subjects.description: Covers four years of secondary education (Forms 1-4); builds on the Junior Heritage-Social Studies foundation with deeper focus on national heritage, culture and patriotism.

subjects.name: Family and Religious Studies
subjects.description: Successor subject to the Infant/Junior 'Family, Religion and Moral Education' (FAREME) strand, covering indigenous religion, Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
